name: Excavation Technique
oracle_text:
Demonstrate (When you cast this spell, you may copy it. If you do, choose an opponent to also copy it. Players may choose new targets for their copies.)
Destroy target nonland permanent. Its controller creates two Treasure tokens.
blocked_sentences: Demonstrate (When you cast this spell, you may copy it. If you do, choose an opponent to also copy it. Players may choose new targets for their copies.)

needs.what: a way for `copy_spell` to put the copy on the stack under a player other than the resolving controller -- a `controller` player-spec on the op that is threaded through to `put_copy_on_stack`, so "choose an opponent to also copy it" makes a copy that opponent controls, resolves for them, and lets them (not you) take the `new_targets` choice
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `copy_spell` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_stack.py) reads only `sid`, `amount` and `new_targets`; it calls `put_copy_on_stack(state, ctx.controller, original, chosen)`, hard-coding the copy's controller to the effect's own controller, and `put_copy_on_stack` builds the StackItem and its backing token object with `controller=controller` from that one argument. `_validate_effect` has no effect-key whitelist, so writing `"controller": "opponent"` on the op would load and be silently ignored -- a copy under the wrong player. `for_each_player` only binds `each_player`; it does not rebind `ctx.controller`, so nesting the op inside it still yields a copy you control. `cast_copy` has the same hard-coded `ctx.controller`. And `_choose_new_targets` asks `ctx.controller`, so even a redirected copy would put the opponent's target choice to the wrong seat.

needs.what: a decision that picks one opponent and binds them for use as a player spec, so "choose an opponent" names a single seat at a multiplayer table rather than the whole `each_opponent` set
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `select_players` resolves `opponent`/`each_opponent` to every opponent at once and offers no chooser; the only ways to name one player are `target`, `controller_of_target`, `controller_of`/`owner_of` and `binding`, all of which read something a target or trigger already produced. Demonstrate's copy is explicitly not targeted, so none of them apply, and at a pod `each_opponent` would hand a copy to every opponent instead of one.
